subject: Private deployment DPA: KMS handoff, subprocessors & data access split

To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@finsecure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Private deployment DPA: KMS handoff, subprocessors & data access split

Hi Sara / FinSecure team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching the latest DPA draft for a private (VPC/on-prem) deployment model. A few items we want to clarify proactively so your legal and infosec teams have the right context:

- Customer-controlled keys: we support CMEK integrations for cloud VPC deployments (you bring keys via your cloud KMS). For on-prem, we offer two patterns: (1) integration with an existing HSM/KMS you manage (we never hold keys), or (2) Redwood-hosted HSM with a customer-controlled escrow key rotation policy.
- Operator access: for private deployments we operate under a strict break-glass process — operator sessions are limited, pre-authorized, and fully logged; we propose adding explicit language about time-limited access and SIEM integration for audit exports.
- Data access boundaries: in VPC/on-prem setups, application-level logs that include PII can be configured to never leave your network; telemetry required for runtime health can be anonymized or routed to your monitoring endpoints.
- Subprocessors: we have a narrow set of subprocessors for build and patching (listed separately). For a fully on-prem install we can commit to a customer-isolation clause that limits Redwood subprocessors from accessing customer data except via pre-agreed maintenance windows with explicit consent.

Requested next steps: can your legal team flag any non-starters in the DPA (attached) and share the specific wording you need around ‘no access / customer keys’ vs. ‘escrow/rotation’? Also, if FinSecure requires EU-only residency for backups, let us know so we can map options.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@finsecure.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Park <d.park@finsecure.com>, FinSecure Legal <legal@finsecure.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA: KMS handoff, subprocessors & data access split

Jordan — thanks for the note and the DPA. A few clarifying bullets from our side after an initial pass (FinSecure InfoSec + Legal):

- Key ownership: FinSecure requires customer-managed keys for all production data in-host (no Redwood-held root keys). We are open to an escrow mechanism only if the escrow is cryptographically split and under a third-party trustee; any automated operator-decrypt ability is a non-starter.
- Operator access: we need explicit SLA on notification timelines for any break-glass invocation, and ability to revoke access programmatically within 5 minutes.
- Subprocessors: please provide the full subprocessors list and the contract language that prevents on-demand access for those subprocessors to our data. For any subprocessors that provide build or patch services, we require white-boxed audit reports and, where possible, temporary creds scoped to the maintenance window.
- Cross‑border/data residency: production backups must be EU-stored if the tenant is provisioned in EU regions. If you plan any telemetry outside the EU, it must be pseudonymized and documented with SCCs.

I've attached our security questionnaire (FinSecure_Security_Q_v2.docx) with several follow-ups inline. Can Vivek or Evelyn confirm the technical feasibility of the escrow + trustee pattern and whether Redwood can provide uninterrupted access logs via a push to our SIEM?

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Legal & Security Program Manager
FinSecure
sara.nguyen@finsecure.com

> Attachment: FinSecure_Security_Q_v2.docx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@finsecure.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 12:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA: KMS handoff, subprocessors & data access split

Hi Sara — thanks for the detailed notes. Technical clarifications and proposed contract language points below:

1) Escrow / trustee model — feasible.
- We can support a threshold (Shamir-style) split where one share is held by FinSecure, one by a neutral trustee, and Redwood holds no full key. During emergency unsealing, the trustee + customer must authorize. We will add explicit DPA language that Redwood cannot unilaterally reconstruct keys.

2) Customer-managed KMS for cloud VPCs — fully supported.
- For GCP/AWS/Azure we integrate with CMEK/HSM endpoints; Redwood never stores plaintext keys.

3) Operator access & revocation — implementation and logs.
- Break-glass: operator sessions require a ticket with two approvers; sessions are time-limited, and we can build a webhook that revokes credentials within <5 minutes when called by your automation.
- Audit exports: we can push syslog/JSON audit streams to an endpoint you control (S3, SIEM) in near real-time. We will include retention and integrity checks (signed exports).

4) Subprocessor constraints — feasible boundaries.
- For fully on-prem installs: all subprocessors are limited to delivering artifacts (binaries/patches) via an authenticated pipeline; they do not receive runtime PII. We can add contractual guarantees requiring scoped, time-limited credentials and post-maintenance audit reports.

5) Cross-border & backups — options.
- If tenant region = EU, backups can be configured to remain in EU regions; snapshots are encrypted with the tenant key. Telemetry can be pseudonymized before leaving the region.

Suggested contract redline snippets (high level):
- "Redwood shall not possess the customer’s production encryption key at any time unless authorized in writing by Customer and subject to escrow procedures described in Appendix X."
- "Operator access for maintenance will require documented Break‑Glass authorization and will be logged; logs will be exported to Customer SIEM with a maximum 24-hour latency and support for immediate revocation via webhook."
- "Subprocessors shall not access runtime customer data outside of explicit, pre-authorized maintenance windows; temporary credentials shall be scoped and audited."

I also attached our internal ops playbook extract (ops_access_playbook.md) that describes the operator session flow and audit fields we capture. Happy to walk through the trustee & escrow options on a technical call.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure 
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com

- Jordan: coordinate calendar invites and collect FinSecure follow-ups.

If that timing works, I’ll schedule the meetings and send calendar invites.
